newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian unit, Thai firm in talks on iron ore plant.
newsitem.headline: Indian unit, Thai firm in talks on iron ore plant.

text.p: India's state-run Orissa Mining Corp (OMC) is negotiating with Thailand's Thai Petrochemical Industry (TPI) to set up a three million tonne iron ore pelletisation plant in the eastern state of Orissa, OMC officials said on Thursday.
The plant is expected to be set up in Darasuan area of Keonjhar district, about 270 kms (170 miles) northwest of the state capital Bhubaneshwar, they said.

The proposed plant, estimated to cost three billion rupees ($85 million), will produce three million tonnes of iron ore pellets, half of which will be exported with the remaining for domestic use, officials said.
OMC officials said preliminary discussions were held when TPI chairman Prachi Leophariatana held talks with Orissa Chief Minister J.B. Patnaik in December.

OMC managing director J.P. Das told Reuters: "The value addition is most welcome. We hope TPI would come forward to set up the joint venture near our mines at Barasuan. We expect the detailed report from TPI any time now."

TPI officials in Thailand confirmed the firm planned to invest in the Orissa project but said discussions were at a "very preliminary" stage. OMC has been asked to come up with an investment proposal soon.
TPI officials said pellets would be used for a steel plant in Thailand. ($1 = 35.86 rupees)
